---
title: "References and credits"
---

IRTistic is built on decades of psychometric research and on the work of the
authors of many R packages. Its estimation code is written from scratch, but
its methods, conventions and many of its design ideas come from the people
listed below. If you use IRTistic in published work, please cite IRTistic
**and** the methodological sources for the procedures you report.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
citation("IRTistic")
```

## Software that inspired and validates IRTistic

**General IRT estimation**

* Chalmers, R. P. (2012). mirt: A multidimensional item response theory package for the R environment. *Journal of Statistical Software, 48*(6), 1-29. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v048.i06
* Rizopoulos, D. (2006). ltm: An R package for latent variable modeling and item response theory analyses. *Journal of Statistical Software, 17*(5), 1-25. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v017.i05
* Mair, P., & Hatzinger, R. (2007). Extended Rasch modeling: The eRm package for the application of IRT models in R. *Journal of Statistical Software, 20*(9), 1-20. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v020.i09
* Robitzsch, A., Kiefer, T., & Wu, M. *TAM: Test analysis modules* [R package]. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=TAM
* Robitzsch, A. *sirt: Supplementary item response theory models* [R package]. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sirt
* Partchev, I., Maris, G., & Hattori, T. *irtoys: A collection of functions related to item response theory* [R package]. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=irtoys

* Bates, D., Mächler, M., Bolker, B., & Walker, S. (2015). Fitting linear mixed-effects models using lme4. *Journal of Statistical Software, 67*(1), 1-48. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v067.i01 (used to validate the Rasch MML estimates during development)

* Linacre, J. M. *Winsteps Rasch measurement computer program*. Winsteps.com. https://www.winsteps.com

## Methodological references, by feature

**Models and estimation** (`irt_fit()`, `irt_scores()`)

* Rasch, G. (1960). *Probabilistic models for some intelligence and attainment tests*. Danish Institute for Educational Research.
* Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee's ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick, *Statistical theories of mental test scores* (pp. 397-479). Addison-Wesley.
* Barton, M. A., & Lord, F. M. (1981). *An upper asymptote for the three-parameter logistic item-response model* (ETS Research Report RR-81-20). Educational Testing Service.
* Samejima, F. (1969). Estimation of latent ability using a response pattern of graded scores. *Psychometrika Monograph Supplement, 34*(4, Pt. 2), No. 17.
* Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. *Psychometrika, 43*(4), 561-573.
* Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. *Psychometrika, 47*(2), 149-174.
* Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 16*(2), 159-176.
* Bock, R. D., & Aitkin, M. (1981). Marginal maximum likelihood estimation of item parameters: Application of an EM algorithm. *Psychometrika, 46*(4), 443-459.
* Warm, T. A. (1989). Weighted likelihood estimation of ability in item response theory. *Psychometrika, 54*(3), 427-450.

**Rasch fit, reliability and dimensionality** (`item_fit()`, `person_fit()`, `reliability()`, `local_dependence()`, `residual_pca()`)

* Wright, B. D., & Stone, M. H. (1979). *Best test design*. MESA Press.
* Wright, B. D., & Masters, G. N. (1982). *Rating scale analysis*. MESA Press.
* Wilson, E. B., & Hilferty, M. M. (1931). The distribution of chi-square. *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 17*(12), 684-688.
* Yen, W. M. (1984). Effects of local item dependence on the fit and equating performance of the three-parameter logistic model. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 8*(2), 125-145.
* Christensen, K. B., Makransky, G., & Horton, M. (2017). Critical values for Yen's Q3: Identification of local dependence in the Rasch model using residual correlations. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 41*(3), 178-194.
* Smith, E. V., Jr. (2002). Detecting and evaluating the impact of multidimensionality using item fit statistics and principal component analysis of residuals. *Journal of Applied Measurement, 3*(2), 205-231.

**Item fit** (`sx2()`)

* Orlando, M., & Thissen, D. (2000). Likelihood-based item-fit indices for dichotomous item response theory models. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 24*(1), 50-64.
* Kang, T., & Chen, T. T. (2008). Performance of the generalized S-X2 item fit index for polytomous IRT models. *Journal of Educational Measurement, 45*(4), 391-406.
* Lord, F. M., & Wingersky, M. S. (1984). Comparison of IRT true-score and equipercentile observed-score "equatings". *Applied Psychological Measurement, 8*(4), 453-461.

**Many-facet Rasch measurement** (`mfrm_fit()`, `facet_report()`, `mfrm_bias()`)

* Linacre, J. M. (1989). *Many-facet Rasch measurement*. MESA Press.
* Eckes, T. (2015). *Introduction to many-facet Rasch measurement: Analyzing and evaluating rater-mediated assessments* (2nd ed.). Peter Lang.
* Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2003). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part I. *Journal of Applied Measurement, 4*(4), 386-422.
* Myford, C. M., & Wolfe, E. W. (2004). Detecting and measuring rater effects using many-facet Rasch measurement: Part II. *Journal of Applied Measurement, 5*(2), 189-227.

**Differential item functioning** (`dif_test()`, `dif_irt()`)

* Mantel, N., & Haenszel, W. (1959). Statistical aspects of the analysis of data from retrospective studies of disease. *Journal of the National Cancer Institute, 22*(4), 719-748.
* Holland, P. W., & Thayer, D. T. (1988). Differential item performance and the Mantel-Haenszel procedure. In H. Wainer & H. I. Braun (Eds.), *Test validity* (pp. 129-145). Lawrence Erlbaum.
* Swaminathan, H., & Rogers, H. J. (1990). Detecting differential item functioning using logistic regression procedures. *Journal of Educational Measurement, 27*(4), 361-370.
* Zumbo, B. D. (1999). *A handbook on the theory and methods of differential item functioning (DIF)*. Directorate of Human Resources Research and Evaluation, Department of National Defense.
* Jodoin, M. G., & Gierl, M. J. (2001). Evaluating Type I error and power rates using an effect size measure with the logistic regression procedure for DIF detection. *Applied Measurement in Education, 14*(4), 329-349.
* Lord, F. M. (1980). *Applications of item response theory to practical testing problems*. Lawrence Erlbaum.

* Meade, A. W. (2010). A taxonomy of effect size measures for the differential functioning of items and scales. *Journal of Applied Psychology, 95*(4), 728-743.
* Candell, G. L., & Drasgow, F. (1988). An iterative procedure for linking metrics and assessing item bias in item response theory. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 12*(3), 253-260.

**Linking and equating** (`irt_link()`, `equate_true_score()`, `score_table()`)

* Stocking, M. L., & Lord, F. M. (1983). Developing a common metric in item response theory. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 7*(2), 201-210.
* Kolen, M. J., & Brennan, R. L. (2014). *Test equating, scaling, and linking: Methods and practices* (3rd ed.). Springer.

**Classification accuracy** (`classification_accuracy()`)

* Rudner, L. M. (2005). Expected classification accuracy. *Practical Assessment, Research & Evaluation, 10*(13).

**Computerized adaptive testing** (`cat_design()`, `cat_simulate()`)

* Weiss, D. J. (1982). Improving measurement quality and efficiency with adaptive testing. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 6*(4), 473-492.
* Kingsbury, G. G., & Zara, A. R. (1989). Procedures for selecting items for computerized adaptive tests. *Applied Measurement in Education, 2*(4), 359-375.
* Chang, H.-H., & Ying, Z. (1996). A global information approach to computerized adaptive testing. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 20*(3), 213-229.
* Chang, H.-H., & Ying, Z. (1999). a-stratified multistage computerized adaptive testing. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 23*(3), 211-222.
* van der Linden, W. J. (1998). Bayesian item selection criteria for adaptive testing. *Psychometrika, 63*(2), 201-216.
* Sympson, J. B., & Hetter, R. D. (1985). Controlling item-exposure rates in computerized adaptive testing. In *Proceedings of the 27th Annual Meeting of the Military Testing Association* (pp. 973-977). Navy Personnel Research and Development Center.
* Chen, S.-Y., Ankenmann, R. D., & Spray, J. A. (2003). The relationship between item exposure and test overlap in computerized adaptive testing. *Journal of Educational Measurement, 40*(2), 129-145.

## Graphics

The colour palette and chart conventions were chosen for legibility in
print and for readers with colour-vision deficiency. Plots are built with
ggplot2 (Wickham, 2016).
